name: Competition Scoring Strategy
description: How IBJJF guard-pass scoring, continuous positional progression and tiebreakers work.
summary: IBJJF scoring depends on the action and qualifying control, as well as the position reached.
overview:
Side control is not automatically a three-point guard pass. IBJJF requires a guard to have been passed and the specified control to be established. Submission holds can affect when the stabilization count starts or whether it is interrupted.

Continuous progression can also score cumulatively. Article 3.4 gives a pass followed by mount as a seven-point example, with the final three-second count continuing the earlier control. At regulation time, equal points are separated by advantages, then fewer penalties, and finally a referee decision if the tie remains.

flashcards.question: Under IBJJF rules, what is the regulation-time tiebreak order after equal points?
flashcards.answer: Compare advantages, then penalties: more advantages wins; if those are tied, fewer penalties wins. A remaining tie goes to the referee decision under Article 2.6.

flashcards.question: Under IBJJF Article 3.4, must a continuous guard-pass-to-mount sequence stop separately in both positions to score?
flashcards.answer: No. With continuous qualifying control through the sequence, the referee counts three seconds at the final scoring position and awards cumulative points; the rulebook’s example totals seven.

flashcards.question: Under IBJJF Article 4.2, does reaching side control always earn guard-pass points?
flashcards.answer: No. A guard must have been passed, followed by the required side or north-south control for three seconds, subject to the scoring rules.
flashcards.answer_line: No; a guard must be passed
